claims.text: The Glean Agent Building Competency certifies partner teams to design, build, govern, and operationalize production-grade Glean Agents that automate workflows and deliver measurable business outcomes.
One competency requirement is completing 5 technical accreditations within the Glean Partner Portal, validated by a Glean Partner Manager.
One competency requirement is completing a Glean-delivered agent building workshop session with your Glean technical team, validated by a Glean Partner Solutions Engineer.
The competency requires building 5 functioning, production-ready agents.
For each competency agent, partners must gather business and technical requirements with the end user, evidenced by a document outlining those requirements.
Competency graduates can design and implement persona-aligned agents, define intents, configure retrieval and guardrails, and construct multi-step agents with clear handoffs and fallbacks.
Advanced agent capabilities include schedule-based triggers, event-driven runs on content changes, and conditional branching and looping to orchestrate robust workflows.
Competency graduates understand best practices for testing and validation of Glean agents.
Competency graduates can deliver enablement and advisory on agents and AI actions.
FND-104 explains the Glean operating model for search, assistants, and agents, and where each construct fits for customer outcomes.
FND-105 provides a decision framework for when to use search, assistant, prompt, agent, action, connector, or integration pattern.
BLD-101 introduces what can be built with agents, actions, APIs, and integration points.
BLD-102 explains actions, MCP, architecture choices, and when to use each approach.
BLD-103 is a hands-on workshop building actions and MCP-backed flows.
BLD-104 is a deeper workshop on agent composition, memory, tool selection, and reusable patterns.
BLD-207 covers how to evaluate prompts and agents, measure quality, and prevent regressions.
BLD-208 covers safety patterns, approval design, escalation boundaries, and production governance for partner-built agents.
SRV-204 covers trace-driven debugging, issue isolation, and clean escalation packages.
SOL-203 designs industry-specific agents that map to common workflows, data sources, and governance requirements.
ACC-104 is the badge for builders who can implement actions, agents, and connectors, assessed by a capstone lab.
